title: The line of teachers' names
hook: the acknowledgments page nobody reads, and an Upanishad that stops to write one
carry: every teacher's name is part of the teaching
tomorrow: what's your lineage, the teacher asks. what if you don't know?

segments.voice: Yesterday, parampara: the teaching passes hand to hand, from the Mundaka's chain back to Brahma to a letter of Paul's handing it forward. Today closes the week, with a list of names.
screen: `BACKWARD, AND FORWARD.` · `TODAY: A LIST OF NAMES.`

segments.voice: Some books end with an acknowledgments page, and it's easy to skip: a list of people the author owes. The Brihadaranyaka Upanishad has pages like that. In the middle of its teaching it stops and says: now, the line of teachers. Then name after name. Why would a sacred text take up room with a list?
screen: `THE PAGE EVERYONE SKIPS.` → `NOW, THE LINE OF TEACHERS.` → `WHY TAKE UP ROOM?`

segments.voice: The word is vamsha, a line. Each name in it received the teaching from the one before: this teacher from that one, from that one, on and on. And the list doesn't stop at a famous sage. It climbs past the human names, and it ends with Brahman, the self-existent, and a bow: salutation to Brahman. So one answer to why: the list is the text's way of saying this came to you by hand, through people who could have dropped it and didn't, and the source of it all is Brahman. Here's the teaching: in Hinduism the names are part of the teaching. In some lineages today, students still chant a verse honoring the whole line, from its first teacher down to their own, before they study. Now the week, from the top. A lake, and a yaksha's question: what's the greatest wonder? A hymn that asks who really knows. Two send-offs, and the four stages of life. Kautsa's gift, and only what he owed. Arjuna, bow fallen: teach me. A chain back to Brahma, and a letter that hands it forward. And today, the line of teachers, written down so nobody forgets who carried it.
screen: `VAMSHA: THE LINE.` · `NAME AFTER NAME, BY HAND.` · `IT ENDS: SALUTATION TO BRAHMAN.` · `THE NAMES ARE PART OF IT.` · `A WEEK AT THE SUMMIT.`

segments.voice: Count, on your fingers, the people who handed you something worth keeping: a story, a prayer, a recipe, a habit, a way of being kind. One finger for each name, slowly. If you run out of fingers, start again.
A lineage: in the Brihadaranyaka, a vamsha, a line of teachers written down name by name, back to Brahman.
Your line: every teacher's name is part of the teaching. A sacred text stopped to say thank you. A week at the summit, held.
